title: A sudden recovery
setting: A weekday evening. Kenji has been off school with a cold. Yuki gets home from work and checks on him. He's on the sofa with his game.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: ケンジ、起きてる？熱、下がった？
lines.kana: けんじ、おきてる？ねつ、さがった？
lines.english: Kenji, you awake? Has your fever come down?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un, sagatta. kinou kusuri nondara, sugu sagatta yo.
lines.ja: うん、下がった。昨日薬飲んだら、すぐ下がったよ。
lines.kana: うん、さがった。きのうくすりのんだら、すぐさがったよ。
lines.english: Yeah, it's down. I took some medicine yesterday and it dropped right away.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yokatta. jaa, kaze mo mou naotta?
lines.ja: よかった。じゃあ、風邪ももう治った？
lines.kana: よかった。じゃあ、かぜももうなおった？
lines.english: Good. So is your cold better now too?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: uun, mada naottenai. ne, ashita mo gakkou ikanakute ii?
lines.ja: ううん、まだ治ってない。ね、明日も学校行かなくていい？
lines.kana: ううん、まだなおってない。ね、あしたもがっこういかなくていい？
lines.english: Nope, not yet. Hey, can I skip school again tomorrow?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e? demo, netsu wa sagatta n da yo ne?
lines.ja: え？でも、熱は下がったんだよね？
lines.kana: え？でも、ねつはさがったんだよね？
lines.english: Huh? But your fever's gone down, right?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. demo, tsukare ga mada torenai n da yo.
lines.ja: うん。でも、疲れがまだ取れないんだよ。
lines.kana: うん。でも、つかれがまだとれないんだよ。
lines.english: Yeah. But I still can't shake this tiredness.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tsukare ga torenai? kyou zutto neteta noni?
lines.ja: 疲れが取れない？今日ずっと寝てたのに？
lines.kana: つかれがとれない？きょうずっとねてたのに？
lines.english: Still tired? You've been asleep all day!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: nete wa nai yo. zutto yoko ni natteta dake.
lines.ja: 寝てはないよ。ずっと横になってただけ。
lines.kana: ねてはないよ。ずっとよこになってただけ。
lines.english: I wasn't asleep. I was just lying down the whole time.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yoko ni natte, nani shiteta no?
lines.ja: 横になって、何してたの？
lines.kana: よこになって、なにしてたの？
lines.english: Lying down and doing what, exactly?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: nani mo shitenai yo. chotto geemu shiteta dake.
lines.ja: 何もしてないよ。ちょっとゲームしてただけ。
lines.kana: なにもしてないよ。ちょっとげーむしてただけ。
lines.english: Nothing. I was just playing a game for a bit.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: chotto? kinou no yoru mo, zutto geemu shiteta yo ne?
lines.ja: ちょっと？昨日の夜も、ずっとゲームしてたよね？
lines.kana: ちょっと？きのうのよるも、ずっとげーむしてたよね？
lines.english: A bit? You were gaming all last night too, weren't you?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.english: Wait, how do you know that?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: zutto kikoeteta yo. yoko ni natte geemu shitetara, tsukare mo torenai yo.
lines.ja: ずっと聞こえてたよ。横になってゲームしてたら、疲れも取れないよ。
lines.kana: ずっときこえてたよ。よこになってげーむしてたら、つかれもとれないよ。
lines.english: I could hear it the whole time. Lie there gaming and of course you're still tired.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: demo, kaze wa honto ni mada naottenai n da yo.
lines.ja: でも、風邪はほんとにまだ治ってないんだよ。
lines.kana: でも、かぜはほんとにまだなおってないんだよ。
lines.english: But my cold really isn't better yet.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sokka. jaa, kono geemu, kaze ga naoru made watashi ga motteru ne.
lines.ja: そっか。じゃあ、このゲーム、風邪が治るまで私が持ってるね。
lines.kana: そっか。じゃあ、このげーむ、かぜがなおるまでわたしがもってるね。
lines.english: I see. Then I'll hang on to this game until your cold's better.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.kana: え！あ、なおった！いまなおった！
lines.english: What? Oh, it's better! It just got better!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto ni? yokatta. jaa, ashita wa gakkou iku ne.
lines.ja: ほんとに？よかった。じゃあ、明日は学校行くね。
lines.kana: ほんとに？よかった。じゃあ、あしたはがっこういくね。
lines.english: Really? Great. So you're going to school tomorrow, then.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: a, un. iku yo. de, geemu wa?
lines.ja: あ、うん。行くよ。で、ゲームは？
lines.kana: あ、うん。いくよ。で、げーむは？
lines.english: Uh, yeah. I'll go. So, can I have my game back?

choices.english: Kenji's fever has come back, so Yuki takes his game and tells him to lie down until he's better.
Kenji is worn out from gaming all night, so Yuki says he can stay home tomorrow if he goes to bed early.
Kenji says his cold isn't better so he can skip school. When Yuki says she'll keep his game until it is, he suddenly feels better, so he's going to school tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Kenji's fever came down yesterday (kusuri nondara, sugu sagatta). Line 4: he says his cold isn't better yet (mada naottenai) and asks to skip school again. Lines 8-13: he wasn't sleeping. He was lying down playing games, so of course he's still tired. Line 15: Yuki will keep the game until his cold is better (kaze ga naoru made). In line 16 it's suddenly better (ima naotta!), so in lines 17-18 he agrees to go to school. A is wrong: his fever is down (lines 2 and 5). Yuki only says she'll keep the game until he's better. B is wrong: Yuki never lets him stay home. She uses the gaming to show he isn't really that sick.

questions.english: Yuki says Kenji has been asleep all day. He answers, "nete wa nai yo. zutto yoko ni natteta dake." What does he mean?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは寝ていましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはねていましたか？

choices.english: He wasn't asleep. He'd just been lying down the whole time.
He'd been sleeping on his side all day, so he didn't sleep well.
He'd slept all day and had only just woken up.

questions.explanation: Line 7: Yuki assumes he slept all day (kyou zutto neteta noni?). Line 8: Kenji corrects her with nete wa nai yo (I wasn't asleep) and zutto yoko ni natteta dake (I was just lying down). Yoko ni naru means lying down to rest, not neru (sleeping). Yuki picks up on it in line 9 (yoko ni natte, nani shiteta no?), and it turns out he was lying there playing his game (line 10). B takes yoko to mean 'side', but yoko ni naru just means lying down, whichever way you face. C is what Yuki assumed, and Kenji says it isn't true.

questions.english: You were in bed with a fever yesterday. Yuki looks in and asks, "kyou wa daijoubu? netsu wa?" (You okay today? How's the fever?) It's come down. Tell her.
questions.kana: きょうはだいじょうぶ？ねつは？
questions.answer: Say your fever has come down, using sagaru in the past: un, netsu sagatta yo.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、薬飲んだら、熱下がった。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I took some medicine and my fever went down.

questions.explanation: A fever comes down by itself with sagaru, so netsu takes ga, which casual speech often drops: netsu sagatta. Yuki asks it that way in line 1, and Kenji answers in line 2 (un, sagatta). Don't use oriru or heru here. Netsu o sageru (with o) means someone bringing the fever down. That's why Kenji puts the medicine in a separate clause: kusuri nondara, sugu sagatta. Yuki only said 'netsu wa?', so you have to supply the verb yourself.

questions.english: Kenji remembers you had a cold last week and asks, "sou ieba, kaze dou?" (Oh yeah, how's your cold?) You're completely over it. Tell him.
questions.answer: Say it's better now, using naoru in the past with mou: un, mou naotta yo.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、風邪もう治った。ありがとう。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm over my cold. Thanks.

questions.explanation: A cold clears up with naoru. Its past form is naotta, and adding mou makes it 'better now'. Kenji says exactly that in line 16 (a, naotta! ima naotta!) once his game is at stake. Mada naottenai (lines 4 and 14) is the 'not yet' answer. Kaze takes ga, which is often dropped. Kaze o naosu (with o) means someone doing the healing, as in hayaku naoshite ne (get well soon).

questions.english: Yuki points out that Kenji's fever is gone. What does Kenji say back?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: But my tiredness hasn't healed yet.
choices.romaji: demo, tsukare ga mada naoranai n da yo.

choices.english: But I still can't shake this tiredness.
choices.romaji: demo, tsukare ga mada torenai n da yo.

choices.english: But my tiredness hasn't gone down yet.
choices.romaji: demo, tsukare ga mada sagaranai n da yo.

questions.explanation: Line 6: tsukare ga mada torenai. Tiredness 'comes off' you (toreru), the way a stain or a button comes off. Yuki repeats it in line 7 and again in line 13 (tsukare mo torenai yo). A is the trap: naoru is for getting over an illness or injury (kaze ga naoru, lines 3 and 16), and tiredness isn't an illness that gets cured. C borrows sagaru from the fever (netsu wa sagatta, line 5). Sagaru is for things that go down on a scale, like a fever, a temperature or a price. Tiredness doesn't go down. It comes off.

newWords.english: until (kaze ga naoru made = until your cold's better)
